newsitem.title: ESTONIA: FINNISH PM AGAINST SPECIAL BALTIC SECURITY ZONE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PM AGAINST SPECIAL BALTIC SECURITY ZONE.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen on Tuesday rejected the idea of a special security zone in the Baltic region to assuage the fears of the Baltic states if they are left out of NATO.
He also told Estonian newspaper Sonumileht that cooperation of different world organisations would contribute to a more secure region.
"The idea of a special security zone in the Baltic and Nordic countries also does not suit us now because such an association would not increase security," Lipponen said.

Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia, which regained their independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991, are all eager to enter NATO as they seek to make sure they never again come under the rule of Moscow.
But their chances of entering the alliance in the first round of expansion are virtually nil as Moscow is vociferously against the idea of their inclusion.
"To improve the security situation here, the cooperation of all organisations -- NATO, OSCE, the European Council, the European Union but also the U.S.A. and Russia -- is needed," Lipponen said.
Finland has several times cautioned that NATO expansion should not create a grey zone in the Baltic region. Finland itself has said it does not want NATO membership.
Lipponen said that Finland neither approves nor disapproves of the Balts' NATO aspirations.

"Finland does not recommend anything to the Baltic countries in the NATO question but we will firmly support the idea that the Baltic countries have the right to decide for themselves, what and whom to join," Lipponen said. REUTER 301044 GMT apr 97
